text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night, hosted by Kestrelmoor at their Flatiron office, was one of the more useful rooms I've been in this year. About 60 of us showed up to hear Priya Raman-Holt (VP Platform, Tallowbrook) and Marcus Feldane (founder, Quillary) talk about the unglamorous part of AI.

My takeaways:

1. Publish a spec instead of building one-offs. Tallowbrook maintains 140 partner integrations with a team of three engineers. Priya's line: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

2. Agent pilots fail at the seam, not the model. Marcus's team wires up data access before choosing a model. Ask the room and you see why: about 40 of the 60 people said an agent pilot at their company had stalled on getting data access.

3. The real debate: who owns the connector? Priya thinks partners should own theirs. Marcus argues the platform has to, or quality drifts. I left unsure, and I think the answer depends on how much you can enforce the spec.

If you're planning an agent rollout, the question to ask first is "can it reach our data?" before "which model?"

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.
